hypothesis: If weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimension during growth, then across ages of growth the log-log slope of median body weight on median stature is close to 3, and the cube of stature reproduces most of the shape of the weight-by-age curve.
pass_criterion: Using NHANES measured stature (BMXHT, cm) and weight (BMXWT, kg) for ages 2-19 y, computed separately for males and females with survey weights: the 1-year-age-bin median weight regressed on median stature on log-log scale gives a slope whose 95% bootstrap CI lies within 2.7-3.3 for both sexes, AND the scaled cube of median stature (k*H^3, k fitted once per sex) explains at least 90% of the variance (R^2 >= 0.90) of median weight across age bins. Both conditions must hold.
fail_criterion: Refuted if, in either sex, the log-log slope point estimate is below 2.5 or above 3.5, or its 95% CI lies entirely outside 2.7-3.3, or the fitted k*H^3 model gives R^2 < 0.80 for median weight across age bins. Results between pass and fail bounds are reported as inconclusive.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimension' is mapped to measured standing height (stature), and 'weight' to measured body mass, treating weight as proportional to volume at roughly constant density. 'Tend to vary as' is read as an approximate power-law exponent near 3 in the cross-sectional age series (a proxy for the average growth trajectory), with 'mainly though not wholly' allowing departures, hence a tolerance band of 2.7-3.3 rather than exactly 3. Modern reinterpretation: the exponent is estimated from population medians by age, not from individual longitudinal tracking; within-age BMI-type scaling (weight ~ height^2) is a different comparison and is not what is tested here.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records examiner-measured standing height and weight by age and sex with survey weights. Fields used: RIDAGEYR (age), RIAGENDR (sex), WTMEC2YR (exam weight), BMXHT (standing height, cm), BMXWT (weight, kg), from the Demographics and Body Measures components, downloadable as SAS XPT files.
